Si ergo quis febricitet; quantum sit refrige-randum, indicat temperamentum naturale, ad quod medicamentis frigidis est reducendus; non neglecta magnitudine morbi & situ partis. Ubi ergo cognoveris quousque refrigerandum sit, remedia accommodata sunt investiganda, eorumque dosis instituenda. & quanquam inexplicabilis sit mensura remediorum in singularibus, nec scientia aliqua comprehensibilis; artificiosa tamen conjectura, usurpanda venit: haec nititur ratione, & experientia. Sicut morbus remedium indicat; ita modum utendi indicant vires, & situs partis affectae. Tempus utendi praescribunt morbi tempora; sicut locum, & vias, corporis figura, & partium situs. Verum quid primo, secundove agen-dum, indicat quod maxime urget. Indicationes a parte affecta sumptae, sunt magni momenti, consid-erantur enim eius temperamentum, sensus, figura, situs, & actio laesa. Tempera-

page.notes: Text is set in roman with italic-free body; the word "ergò" and "à" are printed as shown. Two doubtful readings: "consid-erantur" (line end, hyphen as printed) and "ro sunt" at the top, where the first word is a fragment carried from the line above. The catchword "mento" stands at the right foot after the last line. "N 5" is the gathering signature.
